Make screen gray when this app is open

Makes your phone screen black-and-white while this app is in the foreground.

Color is a major factor in making apps feel rewarding. Removing it makes scrolling feel less engaging.

Requires a one-time setup -- check Settings for the guide.

Automatically sends you to the home screen after N scrolls/taps and/or after a set amount of time in the app -- whichever happens first.

The interaction counter above must be on to kick by scrolls/taps. Kicking by time works either way.

After an auto-close, the app is locked behind a cooldown delay before you can re-open it.

This is the nuclear option for stopping infinite scroll.

Shows a floating counter on screen while you use this app.

For YouTube/Instagram/TikTok: counts how many Reels or Shorts you've scrolled through.

For other apps: counts how many times you've tapped the screen.

Seeing the raw number makes mindless usage feel concrete. The counter turns orange at 10, deep orange at 20, and red at 30.

Choose where this rule applies.

If no features are selected, this rule applies to the whole app when you open it.

If you select Reels, Explore, Shorts, or TikTok Feed, this rule only applies when Nudge detects that feature.

The action still comes from Block Mode above. For example, select Explore + Delay to add a 15 second delay only when opening Explore.

Only apply this rule during specific times.

Select which days the rule is active, and set a start and end time.

Overnight schedules work too -- if the end time is before the start time (e.g. 10 PM to 6 AM), the rule spans midnight.

Displays remaining daily time as a floating overlay while you use this app.

The counter changes color as time runs out:
Green = more than 50% left
Orange = 25-50% left
Red = less than 25% left

Requires a daily time limit to be set.

Set a daily usage budget for this app.

Once you've used the app for this many minutes today, it switches to a hard block for the rest of the day -- regardless of what block mode you chose above.

The block lands as soon as the budget runs out, even if you're still inside the app.

Example: Delay mode + 30 minute limit = you get a countdown each time you open the app, but after 30 minutes of total usage today, the app is fully blocked.

Choose what this rule does when it matches.

Hard Block -- Completely prevents opening the app. You can only go back to the home screen.

Delay -- Shows a countdown timer (5-60 seconds) before letting you in. Gives your brain time to reconsider.

Hold -- Same wait, but the clock only runs while your finger is on the screen. Let go and it starts over.

Breathing -- Guides you through a calming breathing exercise before the app opens.

If multiple matching rules are active, the strongest action wins: Hard Block > Delay > Hold > Breathing.

If multiple active rules match, Nudge uses the strongest action:

Hard Block > Delay > Breathing.

Whole-app rules apply when opening the app. Feature rules apply only when Nudge detects that feature, like Reels, Explore, or Shorts.

Example: Instagram can delay when opened, hard block Reels, and delay Explore.
